subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should OpenClaw relax the default SSRF DNS-answer rule so mixed result sets can proceed after blocked candidates are removed, or should the current any-blocked-answer fail-closed behavior remain intentional?
rationale: The code change is small, but it changes the outbound fetch SSRF boundary and must reflect maintainer security intent rather than an automated policy guess.

options.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
options.body: Allow requests only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into pinned dispatch, and test mixed plus all-blocked cases.

options.title: Keep any-blocked fail-closed
options.body: Document this as intentional strict SSRF behavior and point affected users to trusted proxy or explicit fake-IP/private-network policy where applicable.

options.title: Make mixed polluted DNS opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current default and add or reuse an operator-controlled policy knob for networks with polluted DNS answers.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
recommendation.body: Allow requests only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into pinned dispatch, and test mixed plus all-blocked cases.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant history is the centralized SSRF policy path and IPv6 special-use blocking work tied to this decision.
